title: Session-sticky shadow cutover: Terraform module and automated rollback for VPC runtime upgrades
creator: Ravi Kumar
description:
Problem:
Customers running Redwood Private (VPC) require runtime upgrades with zero observable downtime and deterministic rollback if quality or latency regressions occur. Existing rollout patterns (serial drain or full blue/green swap) either prolong exposure or rely on heavy priming assumptions that don't hold for stateful KV-backed runtimes with session affinity.

Goal:
Deliver a reusable Terraform/IaC module and orchestration pattern to perform parallel, session-sticky shadow replacements of runtime instances inside customer VPCs, with automated health scoring, KV shadow-warmup reconciliation, and an automatic rollback path triggered by configurable health thresholds. The module should be consumable by customers and by Redwood Private's control plane operator.

Scope and non-goals:
- Include Terraform module, CLI hooks, and control-plane integration for automated sequencing.
- Provide synthetic probe suite, latency/cost telemetry gating, and tenant-aware rollback.
- Integrate with existing secret/KMS upgrades and network policies.
- Not in scope: major changes to runtime binary serialization format or storage backend redesign.

Design summary:
1) Shadow nodes: provision ephemeral runtime nodes (same flavor) in the same VPC subnet using a Terraform module. These nodes run a shadow-mode sidecar that mirrors KV reads to a local shadow cache while responding only to mirrored traffic until warmed.
2) Session-sticky cutover: instead of a global traffic flip, router will perform a per-connection (or per-session ID) cutover using a traffic mirror and a short-lived token that shifts new sessions to shadow nodes while existing sticky sessions continue on the old nodes. This preserves session consistency for stateful workloads.
3) Warmup & reconciliation: Run a deterministic KV checkpoint replay to populate shadow node cache. Reconciliation hooks compare checkpointed state and an online sampling of KV keys; discrepancies above a tolerance trigger a hold.
4) Health scoring & gate: Combine synthetic probe pass rate, tail latency delta, error rate, and cache-consistency score into a single rolling health score. The control plane uses this to decide proceed/hold/rollback.
5) Automated rollback: If score breaches lower thresholds within observation window or a customer metric indicates regression, the controller automatically re-routes new sessions back to the previous nodes and tears down shadow nodes. A rollback playbook captures telemetry and attaches the snapshot for post-mortem.

Terraform module responsibilities:
- Create shadow instance group and autoscaler hooks compatible with customer subnets and security groups.
- Attach ephemeral IAM roles and KMS access (scoped).
- Register synthetic probe endpoints and operator-managed config maps.
- Expose output variables: shadow_instance_ids, health_check_url, reconciliation_snapshot_path.

Operator/control-plane hooks:
- A small controller task (stateless) that runs rollout plan: create, warm, mirror, cutover, monitor, finalize.
- Webhook endpoints to accept manual abort/force-commit.
- Idempotent behavior for retries and partial failures.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Module runs in a representative customer VPC and completes an upgrade with zero session-affecting errors in 95% of trials under our internal conftest workload.
- Automated rollback triggers in simulated regression scenarios (e.g., +40% tail latency, 3x error rate) and recovers back to previous state within the SLA window.
- Terraform module outputs and docs published in the private-infra/terraform-modules repo and referenced in Private Console rollout UI.

Security and compliance:
- KMS keys are not copied; module requests temporary decrypt-only roles.
- All SSH access disabled by default; audit logs shipped to customer-configured sinks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Reconciliation false positives: mitigate by sampling tolerances and staged uplift of keys.
- Network ACL differences across customer VPCs: include a preflight network checker in the module.
- Long warmup for very large KV: offer an opt-in snapshot restore path to speed priming.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be applied and destroyed idempotently in a sandbox VPC
Shadow nodes reach warm state (cache reconciliation score >= 0.98) before cutover in test harness
Automated rollback exercises successfully in at least three different simulated regression scenarios
Integration tests added to runtime CI that exercise session-sticky cutover with stateful traffic
Docs and example terraform usage published in private-infra/terraform-modules repo
comments: 2026-02-28 — Ravi Kumar: Initial ticket created after postmortem from customer-vpc incident. Proposed session-sticky shadow pattern to reduce visible impact during runtime upgrades.

2026-03-02 — Samantha Chen: Spiked a PoC in a small sandbox. Shadow nodes + traffic mirror concept works for simple KV sizes but reconciliation is slow for large keyspaces; need snapshot-restore option.
2026-03-04 — Design review (Marco Li): Suggested adding a probabilistic sampler for KV reconciliation to avoid full keyspace scans; approved sampling approach and target error bounds.
2026-03-06 — Security (Priya Menon): Reviewed KMS access pattern; requested ephemeral role approach and audit events for snapshot reads. Added as requirement.

2026-03-09 — Samantha Chen: Implemented terraform module scaffolding in private-infra/terraform-modules/eng/session-sticky-shadow and a controller sketch in runtime/control-plane. Opened PR for module skeleton.

2026-03-11 — Load test results: under conftest workload (10k concurrent sessions) cutover path completed in 8 minutes median, with no session errors in 98% of runs. Tail latency regression observed in one cluster tied to reconciliation I/O; flagged for optimization.
2026-03-12 — Samantha Chen: Added abort webhook, manual override, and initial rollback playbook draft. Next: optimize snapshot restore path and add synthetic probe set to console UI.
